Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ChatGPT Outperforms Crowd-Workers for Text-Annotation Tasks (2303.15056v2) · paper method: The source reports mean within-group label agreement of about 56% for MTurk, 79% for trained annotators, 91% for ChatGPT at temperature 1 and 97% at 0.2; it also records a relevance-task failure from missing prompt examples and leaves multilingual/other-model evaluation for future work.

  • Repeated model-output agreement is not independent human agreement or evidence that labels are correct.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ChatGPT Outperforms Crowd-Workers for Text-Annotation Tasks (2303.15056v2) · paper method: The MTurk comparison requires Masters status, over 90% approval and at least 50 approved HITs, US location, no more than 20% of a task’s tweets per worker, and two workers per tweet; this describes that recruitment protocol rather than an unscreened crowd baseline.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ChatGPT Outperforms Crowd-Workers for Text-Annotation Tasks (2303.15056v2) · paper method: Accuracy is agreement with trained human annotations only on texts where both trained annotators agreed; within the four study datasets the source reports ChatGPT exceeding MTurk accuracy by about 25 percentage points on average. This restricted gold denominator excludes trained-rater disagreement.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

ChatGPT Outperforms Crowd-Workers for Text-Annotation Tasks (2303.15056v2) · paper method: The study applies the same codebook wording to trained political-science students, screened US MTurk workers and gpt-3.5-turbo. API annotations were collected in March–May 2023, with two runs at each temperature (1 and 0.2), a fresh chat per tweet and one tweet per query.
